scope: Read-only diagnosis first; placeholders require operator substitution and review.

trees.title: Boot or emergency mode
trees.symptom: The host fails normal boot or enters emergency mode.
preconditions: Record the console error and current boot target.
Use the console or approved out-of-band path; do not troubleshoot a failed boot only over SSH.

branches.when: The console names a failed mount or dependency
branches.next: Continue with the fstab tree; do not bypass an unknown storage failure.

branches.when: The console names a failed service
branches.next: Inspect the named unit and its dependency failure before changing targets.
Preserve the boot journal and escalate before editing bootloader or initramfs state.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.

trees.title: Broken /etc/fstab
trees.symptom: Boot or mount processing fails after a filesystem-table change.
preconditions: Capture the current file and mount state before editing.

branches.when: Syntax or option error is suspected
branches.next: Correct only the identified row, then re-run findmnt verification.
Confirm the intended UUID/device with inventory; do not substitute a guessed device.
Stop write activity and follow the filesystem-specific offline repair procedure.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.

trees.title: DNF or RPM failure
trees.symptom: Package operations report locks, dependency conflicts, repository failures, or transaction errors.
preconditions: Do not delete RPM database lock files.
Record the requested package and repository configuration.

branches.when: Another package process may be active
branches.next: Identify and allow the legitimate transaction to finish; do not kill it blindly.
Check the named repository URL, entitlement, DNS, proxy and time state.
Preserve the solver output and review package provenance before using remove, downgrade or distro-sync.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.

trees.title: NetworkManager connectivity
trees.symptom: A connection is down, has the wrong address, or activation interrupts reachability.
preconditions: Maintain console or out-of-band access before changing the active management profile.
Record all saved and active connection profiles.

branches.next: Identify the saved profile intended for the device before activation.

branches.when: Address, route or DNS is wrong
branches.next: Compare saved profile, active state and approved network plan; do not infer DNS from address configuration.
Use console access to reactivate the captured prior profile.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.

trees.title: Firewalld reachability
trees.symptom: A service is unreachable or a rule appears ineffective after a firewall change.
preconditions: Record source and destination addresses, protocol, port and intended zone.
Keep an existing management session and console recovery path.

branches.when: Runtime and permanent state may differ
branches.next: Compare the exact zone and exact rule in both stores.
Recover with --remove-rich-rule using the exact original rule; do not add a contradictory rule.

branches.when: The rule is present but traffic fails
branches.next: Verify the service listener and network path before changing the firewall again.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.

trees.title: LVM or filesystem capacity
trees.symptom: A filesystem is full, an LV is missing, or storage layout differs from expectation.
preconditions: Stop before any pvcreate, vgcreate, lvremove, filesystem creation or repair.
Record device identity, holders, mounts and LVM membership.

branches.next: Determine whether blocks, inodes or deleted-open files are responsible before extending storage.
Match serial, path and membership to inventory before any write.
Stop writes and use the filesystem-specific, offline recovery runbook.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.
trees.source: man 8 lvs; man 8 findmnt; filesystem-specific repair documentation

trees.title: SELinux AVC denial
trees.symptom: An operation fails and the audit log contains an AVC denial.
preconditions: Record the exact application action, path and domain.

branches.when: A recent denial matches the failure
branches.next: Correct labeling or supported policy configuration; review suggested policy changes rather than applying them blindly.
Use restorecon only after confirming the expected label and file purpose.
Continue diagnosing the application; do not disable SELinux to manufacture a different symptom.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.
trees.source: man 8 ausearch; man 8 restorecon; Red Hat SELinux guide

trees.title: Chrony and time synchronization
trees.symptom: The clock is unsynchronized, sources are unreachable, or skew breaks authentication.
preconditions: Record the current clock, timezone and configured sources.
Large time steps can disrupt applications; do not force one without an approved window.

branches.next: Identify whether chronyd is running and whether any source is selectable.
Check DNS, route and UDP/123 policy for the configured source.
Review parsed configuration before restart; preserve the prior file.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.
trees.source: man 1 chronyc; man 8 chronyd; man 5 chrony.conf

trees.title: Rsyslog forwarding and receipt
trees.symptom: Local logs exist but remote receipt is absent or delayed.
preconditions: Record expected source identity, destination, protocol and port.
Do not include secrets or sensitive log bodies in tickets.

branches.next: Fix reported syntax errors before reload.
Verify queue/action errors and destination reachability.

branches.when: Transport works but events are not searchable
branches.next: Confirm source-attributed receipt at the collector; a healthy sender alone is not end-to-end evidence.

trees.escalate: Stop and preserve observed output when device identity, recovery access, approved state, or change authority is uncertain.
trees.source: man 8 rsyslogd; man 1 logger; RHEL logging documentation
